subject: Emit priming & heartbeat probe — TTFT / streaming requirements follow-up
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Ari Lyman <ari@speedpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Emit priming & heartbeat probe — TTFT / streaming requirements follow-up

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the SpeedPay infra and payments folks. I wanted to capture the technical asks and next steps we agreed on so we can scope a short TTFT + streaming probe: 

Summary of asks from SpeedPay (as we captured):
- Target time-to-first-token (TTFT) goal: 120–150ms p95 for short intents (10–20 tokens) under normal load.
- Sustained throughput target for the probe: 200 concurrent requests, burst to 500 for 30s.
- Streaming mode: server-sent events (SSE) preferred for client simplicity; websocket fallback acceptable if SSE shows instability.
- Chunk cadence: prefer small initial priming chunk (10–15 tokens) within the first TTFT window, followed by regular heartbeats every ~200ms for long outputs to keep UI responsive.
- Fallbacks: auto-fallback to smaller model variant when queueing >300 requests to preserve p95 TTFT.

Immediate next steps we agreed: 
1) SpeedPay to share representative payloads and a short traffic sketch (attached example-payloads.json).
2) Redwood will propose a 3-day lab probe with measurement harness (we'll include SSE/WS toggles, synthetic concurrency ramp, and KV prefix priming tests).
3) Confirm the acceptance criteria: p95 TTFT <= 150ms and packet heartbeat jitter < 50ms across 95% of packets.

Can you confirm the bullets above reflect your priorities and attach the payloads + any network egress constraints? Once we have that we will schedule the lab window and share the probe plan spreadsheet.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com

From: Ari Lyman <ari@speedpay.com>

Cc: SpeedPay Platform Team <infra@speedpay.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emit priming & heartbeat probe — TTFT / streaming requirements follow-up

Thanks Grace — this matches our takeaways. Quick clarifications and constraints from our side: 
- The 120–150ms p95 is our ideal for chrome-based web checkout flows; mobile clients can tolerate up to 200ms p95.
- For the probe, our backend will generate ~75 RPS steady state with peaks up to 220 RPS (client-side fanout to many tabs may create bursts). That maps roughly to your 200 concurrent request target during steady plus short spikes.
- Network: all traffic originates from our us-west-2 VPC. We will whitelist Redwood demo IPs but cannot route through a private peering for the first run. Expect typical internet egress variance (10–25ms additional).
- We attached representative sample payloads and a short CSV of request-size distribution.

Two asks before you run the lab: 
1) Will you include a KV prefix priming test to simulate cached context at cold-start? We believe priming will materially affect TTFT for our top-10 intents.
2) Can you include an SSE connection drop test (10% random disconnect at 60s) to validate automatic websocket fallback behavior?

Attached: example-payloads.json, request-sizes.csv

—Ari
Ari Lyman, Head of Platform Engineering
SpeedPay

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Ari Lyman <ari@speedpay.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Emit priming & heartbeat probe — TTFT / streaming requirements follow-up

Thanks Ari — details helpful. A few technical notes and proposed probe knobs from the Redwood runtime team: 

Probe components we propose to run (3-day lab):
- Cold-start TTFT sweep: run synthetic single-request latency tests across model variants (fp16 / int8) and with/without KV prefix priming.
- Continuous concurrency ramp: 50 -> 200 concurrent sessions over 45 minutes; three bursts to 500 concurrent sessions for 30s each.
- Streaming cadence experiment: test three cadence profiles — (A) small prime 12 tokens + 200ms heartbeat, (B) prime 20 tokens + 300ms heartbeat, (C) no priming + 150ms heartbeat — measure p95 TTFT, jitter, and user-visible first-chunk size.
- SSE drop and websocket fallback: simulate 10% connection termination at 60s; verify that websocket fallback restores stream within 300ms and preserves partial output.
- Network variance emulation: add 10–30ms extra egress to match your range.

Acceptance criteria (we will measure per your objectives):
- p95 TTFT <= 150ms for desktop flows (we'll report mobile separately).
- For streaming: first chunk emitted within the TTFT window (<= 150ms), and heartbeat jitter < 50ms p95.
- Under burst conditions, service should maintain availability; if p95 degrades >30% we record failover to smaller model variant and note QoE change.

Questions for SpeedPay before we finalize schedule: 
1) Which exact model family do you want us to use for baseline (we have Mesa-7B int8 and Atlas-13B fp16). Baseline choice affects absolute TTFT numbers.
2) Do you want us to test SSE only or include websocket as a first-class mode? (we can run both in parallel but it increases probe runtime).

Once we have model choice and confirm probe window (we prefer Wed–Fri this week), we'll share the lab harness link and the measurement dashboard.

- Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Emit priming & heartbeat probe — TTFT / streaming requirements follow-up

Perfect — thanks Ari and Aditya. SpeedPay confirms Atlas-13B fp16 as baseline for the probe and wants both SSE + websocket tested (SSE primary).

We booked the lab window: Wed 14 Apr 14:00 UTC — Fri 16 Apr 14:00 UTC. Redwood will: 
- Run the three cadence profiles and the cold-start sweep.
- Share live dashboard and a short runbook (heartbeat thresholds, failover triggers, and log locations).

Action items: 
- SpeedPay: confirm whitelist CIDR for demo and confirm a point-of-contact for in-window calls (we'll need a 20-min check-in at start and one at end of each day).
- Redwood: publish the lab harness link and measurement dashboard by EOD today and upload the probe schedule into the shared Drive link above.

I'll follow up with the calendar invites and the runbook. Looking forward to the probe — should give good signal against your TTFT target.

Thanks,
Grace
